info.title: Agent Actions HTTP endpoints
info.description: Use AI and LLMs to interact with and modify your content.

post.description:
Sends an instruction request to Generate for a specific dataset.

Examples and implementation details can be found in the [Generate documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions/generate-quickstart).

requestBody.description:
The body must contain either a `targetDocument` or `documentId` property.
These properties are mutually exclusive.

post.description:
Transforms a source document. By default, the changes are written to the source document. To write them to a different document, set `targetDocument`.

Examples and implementation details can be found in the [Transform documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions/transform-quickstart).

Translates a source document. By default, the translation is written to the source document. To write it to a different document, set `targetDocument`.

Examples and implementation details can be found in the [Translate documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions/translate-quickstart).

post.summary: Prompt the LLM for a response
post.description:
Prompt the LLM for a response. Does not interact with documents beyond fetching content as context when requested.
Use for tasks that don't require manipulating documents, such as generating details that you may want to use with other Agent Actions.

Examples and implementation details can be found in the [Prompt documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions/prompt-quickstart).

200.description: Request was successful. Returns `text/plain` when `format` is `string`, and the JSON the instruction asks for when `format` is `json`.

post.summary: Make a schema-aware patch to a document
post.description:
A schema-aware patch API that validates the provided paths and values against the target schema.
This operation doesn't use an LLM and only uses regular Sanity billing for API requests.
Unknown properties in the request body are rejected with a `400`.

Examples and implementation details can be found in the [Patch documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions/patch-quickstart).

PathSegment.title: Path Segment
PathSegment.description: A single path segment, either a field name or an array item key.

PathArray.title: Path Array
PathArray.description: A list of path segments, from the document root down.

Path.title: Path
Path.description:
A document path: either a single path segment, or an array of segments.

Examples:
```json
"body"  // Field name
{ "_key": "section1" }  // Array item by key
["body", { "_key": "section1" }, "title"]  // Path array
```

Operation.title: Operation Type
Operation.description:
Sets the default operation for all paths in the target.

Operation types:
  - 'set': Overwrites and replaces the full field value.
  - 'append':
    - array fields: Appends new items to the end of the array.
    - string fields: Appends new content to the end of the string.
    - text fields: Appends new content to a new line after the existing content.
    - number fields: The sum of the new value and the existing value.
    - Other field types not mentioned will use `set` instead.
  - 'mixed': (Default) Sets non-array fields, and appends array fields.

Use `include` to override the default `operation` for specific paths.

Nested fields inherit the operation of their parent, and fall back
to the top level target operation unless otherwise specified.

PatchOperation.title: Patch Operation Type
PatchOperation.description:
Determines how the target path will be patched.
- `'set'`: an *overwriting* operation: sets the full field value for primitive targets, and merges the provided value with existing values for objects
- `'append'`:
    - array fields: appends new items to the end of the array,
    - string fields: '"existing content" "new content"'
    - text fields: '"existing content"\\n"new content"'
    - number fields: existing + new
    - other field types not mentioned will set instead (dates, url)
- `'mixed'`:  sets non-array fields, and appends to array fields
- `'unset'`: removes whatever value is on the target path

All operations except unset require a `value`.

#### Appending in the middle of arrays
To append to an array, use the 'append' operation and provide an array value with one or more array items.
`target: {path: ['array'], operation: 'append', value: [{_type: 'item', _key: 'a'}]}` will append the items in the value to the existing array.
To insert in the middle of the array, use `target: {path: ['array', {_key: 'appendAfterKey'}], operation: 'append', value: [{_type: 'item', _key: 'a'}]}`.
Here, `{_type: 'item', _key: 'a'}` will be appended after the array item with key `'appendAfterKey'`
It is optional to provide a _key for inserted array items; if one isn't provided, it will be generated.

TypeConfig.title: Type Configuration
TypeConfig.description:
Configure which schema types to include or exclude from the instruction: array item types, or all fields of a type directly under the target path.
`include` and `exclude` are mutually exclusive.

Example:
```json
{
  "include": ["text", "image", "video"]
}
```

maxPathDepth.description:
The maximum depth of the document paths the instruction can write to.
When `target` is omitted, Transform and Translate use a depth of 12.
Depth is based on field path segments:
- `title` has a depth of 1
- `author.name` has a depth of 2
- `array[_key="123"].title` has a depth of 3

Use caution when setting this value too high in studios with recursive document schemas
as it may cause performance and response quality issues.

BaseInclude.title: Base Include Configuration
BaseInclude.description:
By default, all children up to the maxPathDepth are included.

When include is specified, only segments explicitly set in `include` will be included.
Each `include` entry is either a single path segment, or an object with a `path` and its own settings.

Target.title: Target Configuration

GenerateTarget.title: Generate Target Configuration
GenerateTarget.description: Defines which parts of the document will be affected by the Generate instruction.

Exclude.title: Exclude Configuration
Exclude.description:
Define fields or array items to exclude from the instruction. Any omitted fields or array items are implicitly included.
By default, all children up to the maxPathDepth are included.

Example:
```json
["metadata", "draft", { "_key": "tempSection" }]
```

TransformOperation.title: Transform Operation Type
TransformOperation.description:
Sets the default operation for all paths in the target.

Operation types:
  - 'set': (Default) Overwrites and replaces the full field value.
  - 'image-description': Lets the transform action select an image asset, select a field, and describe the image in the field. You can also set an `imageUrl` to describe remote images.

Use `include` to override the default `operation` for specific paths.

Nested fields inherit the operation of their parent, and fall back
to the top level target operation unless otherwise specified.

type.description: Use to describe an image asset. It will find an adjacent asset if located in the image path. For external paths, use sourcePath. For remote images, use imageUrl.

imageUrl.description: The URL of the image to describe. Must use HTTPS. Can't be combined with `sourcePath`.

sourcePath.description: The path to the image asset to describe, as an array of path segments.

TransformTargetDocument.description:
The target document to transform and the operation to perform. 
If omitted, the source document (`documentId`) will be used as the target.

oneOf.title: Edit Document
oneOf.description: Get the document with the given `_id`.

operation.description: Directly edit the document with the given `_id`.

oneOf.title: Create Document
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id`. If no `_id` is provided, a new draft document is created.

oneOf.title: Create If Not Exists
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id` if it does not exist.

operation.description: Create a new document with the given `_id` if it does not exist. If the document already exists, the existing document is used as the basis for the changes.

oneOf.title: Create Or Replace
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id`. If the document already exists, it is replaced.

operation.description: Create a new document with the given `_id`. If the document already exists, it is replaced with the new document content.

GenerateTargetDocument.description: The operation to perform and the target document to transform.

oneOf.title: Edit Document
oneOf.description: Get the document with the given `_id`.

oneOf.title: Create Document
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id`.

oneOf.title: Create If Not Exists
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id` if it does not exist. If the document already exists, the existing document is used as the basis for the changes.

oneOf.title: Create Or Replace
oneOf.description: Create a new document with the given `_id`. If the document already exists, it is replaced.

schemaId.description: The schema identifier reported by `sanity deploy` or `sanity schema deploy`.

conditionalPaths.description: Allows the instruction to modify conditional `readOnly` or `hidden` fields. Does not apply to fields explicitly set as hidden or readOnly in the schema.

defaultReadOnly.description: When false, forces all conditional readOnly fields to be writable.

defaultHidden.description: When false, forces all conditional hidden fields to be writable.

paths.description: Override the default behavior of individual conditional paths.

path.description: Must be the full document path as an array of path segments, regardless of the path defined in `target`.

readOnly.description: When false, the field is writable.

hidden.description: When false, the field is writable.

AgentActionWriteOptions.description: `noWrite: true` and `async: true` can't be combined.

forcePublishedWrite.description:
Set to true to mutate published documents. By default, Agent Actions will never mutate a published document. They will use a draftId if a publishedId is provided.
Operations on drafts receive initial state from the published document, if no draft exists. If a draft exists, it is used as the initial state.
The returned `_id` will be that of the modified document.

Documents set to `liveEdit: true` will be mutated as if `forcePublishedWrite: true`.

noWrite.description: When true, documents aren't created or mutated.

async.description: When true, requests occur in the background. True is incompatible with `noWrite: true`.

temperature.description: Controls the level of variance in the response. A higher value returns more variation in responses, while a lower value returns more predictable responses. Defaults to `0.3` for Generate, and `0` for Transform and Translate.

localeSettings.description:
When provided with locale settings, Agent Actions write to `date` and `datetime` fields.
Otherwise, those fields are ignored.

locale.description: A valid Unicode [BCP 47 locale identifier](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl#getcanonicalocales). This will affect how natural language time and date phrases are parsed and presented.

timeZone.description: A valid [IANA time zone identifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones). This will ensure dates and times are interpreted correctly relative to the user's local time.

Parameter.title: Instruction Parameter
Parameter.description:
Parameter values available to reference in the instruction.

There are four types of parameters:
- `constant`: Set a static value. A plain string is shorthand for a constant parameter.
- `field`: Target a field in the document to set the parameter to its value
- `groq`: Set the parameter to the result of a GROQ query
- `document`: Set the parameter to the value of the entire document

FieldParam.title: Field Parameter
FieldParam.description:
Set the parameter to the value of the field at the given path.
If no `documentId` is provided, the current document is used. Note: for prompt request, the documentId is required.

perspective.description: The perspective to run the query with.

DocumentParam.title: Document Parameter
DocumentParam.description:
Set the parameter to the value of the entire document.
If no `documentId` is provided, the current document is used. Note: for prompt request, the documentId is required.

documentId.description: The ID of the source document to translate.

styleGuide.description: A style guide for the translation.
styleGuide.example: Use a formal tone and avoid using contractions.

protectedPhrases.description:
A list of phrases that should not be translated. 
Use this instead of the style guide for phrases or words you want the translation to leave unchanged.

languageFieldPath.description:
Set this to the path of the field where the language code is set in your document schema.
This will ensure the new document has the correct language code added after translation. 
This has no effect on the translation process.

documentId.description: The ID of the source document to transform.

Set to the document ID of the document you want to modify. 
This is the shorthand equivalent of `targetDocument: { _id: '123', operation: 'edit' }`.
Mutually exclusive with `targetDocument`.

Instruction.title: Instruction Text
Instruction.description: Describes the instruction. Reference `instructionParams` using the `$variable` syntax.
Instruction.example: Create a new document with a title like $title, that matches the style of $externalTitle, and generate content based on the $backgroundContext.

InstructionParams.title: Instruction Parameters
InstructionParams.description:
Parameter values available to reference in the instruction.

There are four types of parameters:
- `constant`: Set a static value. Ex: `paramName: { type: 'constant', value: 'New title'}`, or the shorthand `paramName: 'New title'`
- `field`: Target a field in the document to set the parameter to its value. Also takes an optional `documentId` to target a field in a different document. Ex: `paramName: { type: 'field', path: 'poster'}`
- `groq`: Set the parameter to the result of a GROQ query. Ex: `paramName: { type: 'groq', query: '*[_type == $docType]', params: { 'docType': 'article'} }`
- `document`: Set the parameter to the value of the entire document. If no `documentId` is provided, the current document is returned. Prompt requests require `documentId` for `field` and `document` parameters. Ex: `paramName: { type: 'document', documentId: '123'}`

IncludeInstruction.title: Include Instruction Text
IncludeInstruction.description: Describes the instructions for the included targets. References the top-level `instructionParams` using the `$variable` syntax.

TransformTarget.title: Transform Target Configuration
TransformTarget.description: Defines which parts of the document will be affected by the Transform instruction.

TransformInclude.title: Transform Include
TransformInclude.description: Defines which parts of the document will be included in the Transform instruction.

title.description: The human-friendly name for the language.

InitialValues.title: Initial Values
InitialValues.description: Define any initial values for the document. Similar to initial value templates in Studio, this is useful for setting fields to pre-determined values directly without going through the LLM.

error.description: Error name. For validation errors, a summary of the failed validations.

message.example: Incompatible parameters: async and noWrite cannot both be true

statusMessage.description: HTTP status text. Only present on request validation errors.

details.description: The individual validation issues. Only present on request validation errors.

organization.description: The organization that disabled AI features. Only present on that `403` error.

temperature.description: The temperature to use for the prompt. Controls how much variance there will be in responses.

format.description: The format of the response. If `json`, the instruction must include the word "json", in any letter case.

documentId.description:
The ID of the document to patch.
Either `documentId` or `targetDocument` is required. They're mutually exclusive.

value.description: The value to write at `path`. Required for every operation except `unset`. Can't be `null`.

Document.description: Request was successful, returning the resulting document.

schema.description: A Sanity document shape. Additional properties depend on the document schema.

_createdAt.description: The creation date of the document.

_updatedAt.description: The last update date of the document.

_rev.description: The revision number of the document.

TransformedDocument.description:
Request was successful, returning the resulting document.
When some paths failed or were skipped, the response includes the `x-transform-*` headers.

x-transform-succeeded.description: Number of paths that were transformed. Only present when paths failed or were skipped.

x-transform-failed.description: Number of paths that failed. Only present when paths failed or were skipped.

x-transform-skipped.description: Number of paths that were skipped. Only present when paths failed or were skipped.

x-transform-aborted.description: Whether the request was aborted. Only present when paths failed or were skipped.

Accepted.description: Request accepted and processed asynchronously (`async: true`). Returns the ID of the document that will be modified.

BadRequest.description: Bad request. The request body is invalid, contains incompatible parameters, or uses an API version other than `vX`.

value.message: Incompatible parameters: async and noWrite cannot both be true
Agent Actions are only available on apiVersion vX

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. The token is missing, invalid, or expired.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden. AI features are disabled for the project's organization.

example.error: AI features have been disabled at this organization's request.

NotFound.description: Not Found. The document or the schema could not be found.

value.message: Schema for schemaId '_.schemas.default' could not be not found.

LimitReached.description: Too Many Requests. The plan or Agent Actions budget limit has been reached.

example.message: Please change the plan or Agent Actions budget in sanity.io/manage.

LLMError.description: Internal Server Error. The language model request failed.

example.message: One of our API providers failed to execute a task. Please try again later.

BearerAuth.description: A Sanity API token or a user session token.
